title: Startup Funding Climate This Week
shortAnswer: Funding is tighter when short-term rates sit above about 3.5%, which is where the pause line is drawn.
directAnswer: Decide the worst terms you would accept before you start a raise, and tighten them while funding pressure is above its line.

keyword: is it risk-on or risk-off for startups
title: Is It Risk-On or Risk-Off for Startups?
shortAnswer: Speed up when risk appetite is above its line, slow down when it is below; the yield curve moves risk appetite and funding pressure together.
directAnswer: Move faster on the bets you can stop, and write the stop condition down first.

keyword: should startups hire engineers right now
title: Should Startups Hire Engineers Right Now?
shortAnswer: Only for roles that pay back inside 12 months; hold the rest.
directAnswer: Approve only roles tied to delivery reliability or near-term revenue impact.

title: Should Startups Slow Roadmap Expansion?
shortAnswer: Yes: slow the new scope, not the work you have already promised.
directAnswer: Keep the roadmap work that moves retention or revenue within the quarter; pause new platform bets until the scores are back across their resume lines.

title: Should Startups Raise Capital Now?
shortAnswer: Raise now if you have under 12 months of cash or the round would take you past 24; otherwise wait for terms you would keep.
directAnswer: If your plan for the next 12 months needs the money, start now, while you can still say no to bad terms.

title: When Should Startups Cut Burn?
shortAnswer: Cut burn when funding pressure crosses its pause line and risk appetite is falling at the same time.
directAnswer: Decide now which spend you would cut, so the cut is ready before funding pressure crosses its line.

keyword: should we freeze hiring or selectively hire
title: Should We Freeze Hiring or Selectively Hire?
shortAnswer: Hire selectively, with the stop condition written before the first offer.
directAnswer: Approve only reliability and revenue roles, each with its own payback window and pause condition.

keyword: should we expand sales headcount now
title: Should We Expand Sales Headcount Now?
shortAnswer: Only where win rates are holding and each rep pays back inside 12 months.
directAnswer: Add reps in small groups, each group only after the previous one's win rate has held and cash allows it.

keyword: should we delay new product lines
title: Should We Delay New Product Lines?
shortAnswer: Delay a new product line unless customers are already asking for it.
directAnswer: Keep the core roadmap shipping; start a new line only after an adoption milestone and a payback figure.

keyword: how fast should we scale go to market
title: How Fast Should We Scale Go-To-Market?
shortAnswer: Add sales and marketing spend in steps, not all at once.
directAnswer: Raise spend and hiring one step per milestone, and pull the step back the moment conversion or payback slips.

keyword: how to brief executives on market conditions
title: How to Brief Executives on Market Conditions
shortAnswer: Lead with what changed, the rule it changes, and what would change the guidance.
directAnswer: Keep it to one screen: the reading, the one rule it changes, and the number that would change the guidance again.
audience: Chief of staff, strategy, and ops
